summary.en: Planning your money ahead, and checking how reality compares to the plan.
summary.bs: Planiranje novca unaprijed i provjera koliko se stvarnost slaže s planom.

concepts.youtubeQuery: how to make a business budget explained simply

en.one: A budget is a plan for how much money you expect to earn and spend.
en.explain: You write down expected income and every expected cost, usually month by month for a year. It turns goals into numbers and sets limits before the money is spent.
en.example: A small online shop plans €5,000 sales per month, €2,000 for products, €500 for ads, €300 for software and €1,200 for wages. It plans to keep €1,000 a month.
en.why: Without a budget, spending decisions are guesses. With one, you can say no to things that do not fit the plan.
en.mixup: A budget is not a prediction that must come true. It is a plan you compare against.

bs.one: Budget (budžet) je plan koliko novca očekuješ zaraditi i potrošiti.
bs.explain: Zapišeš očekivane prihode i svaki očekivani trošak, obično mjesec po mjesec za godinu dana. Pretvara ciljeve u brojeve i postavlja granice prije nego što se novac potroši.
bs.example: Mala online prodavnica planira 5.000 € prodaje mjesečno, 2.000 € za robu, 500 € za reklame, 300 € za softver i 1.200 € za plate. Planira zadržati 1.000 € mjesečno.
bs.why: Bez budžeta, odluke o trošenju su nagađanje. S budžetom možeš reći ne stvarima koje se ne uklapaju u plan.
bs.mixup: Budžet nije predviđanje koje se mora ostvariti. To je plan s kojim se porediš.

concepts.youtubeQuery: fixed vs variable costs explained simply

en.one: Fixed costs stay the same no matter how much you sell. Variable costs go up and down with sales.
en.explain: Rent, insurance and software subscriptions are usually fixed. Materials, packaging and delivery are variable, because every extra sale needs more of them.
en.example: A pizza place pays €2,000 rent whether it sells 10 or 1,000 pizzas (fixed). Each pizza needs €2 of ingredients (variable).
en.why: Knowing which costs are which tells you how risky a slow month is, and how much profit each extra sale brings.
en.mixup: Fixed does not mean forever. Rent can change next year. It is fixed only in the short term.

bs.one: Fiksni troškovi ostaju isti bez obzira koliko prodaš. Varijabilni troškovi rastu i padaju s prodajom.
bs.explain: Kirija, osiguranje i pretplate na softver su obično fiksni. Materijal, ambalaža i dostava su varijabilni, jer svaka dodatna prodaja traži više toga.
bs.example: Picerija plaća 2.000 € kirije bez obzira da li proda 10 ili 1.000 pica (fiksno). Svaka pica traži 2 € sastojaka (varijabilno).
bs.why: Kad znaš koji su troškovi koji, znaš koliko je slab mjesec rizičan i koliko dobiti donosi svaka dodatna prodaja.
bs.mixup: Fiksno ne znači zauvijek. Kirija se iduće godine može promijeniti. Fiksna je samo kratkoročno.

concepts.youtubeQuery: financial forecast vs budget explained simply

en.one: A forecast is your best guess of what will actually happen, updated as you learn more.
en.explain: The budget is set at the start of the year. A forecast changes every month or quarter, using real results so far. It answers: given what we know now, where will we end up?
en.example: The shop budgeted €60,000 sales for the year. After a strong spring, the forecast is updated to €68,000.
en.why: Forecasts help you spot cash problems early and decide when to hire, buy stock or slow down.
en.mixup: A forecast is not the same as a budget. The budget is the target. The forecast is the expected reality.

bs.one: Forecast (prognoza) je tvoja najbolja procjena onoga što će se stvarno desiti, koju ažuriraš kako saznaješ više.
bs.explain: Budžet se postavi na početku godine. Prognoza se mijenja svaki mjesec ili kvartal, na osnovu stvarnih rezultata do tada. Odgovara na pitanje: s obzirom na ono što sada znamo, gdje ćemo završiti?
bs.example: Prodavnica je budžetirala 60.000 € prodaje za godinu. Nakon jakog proljeća, prognoza se ažurira na 68.000 €.
bs.why: Prognoze ti pomažu da rano uočiš probleme s novcem i odlučiš kad zaposliti, kupiti robu ili usporiti.
bs.mixup: Prognoza nije isto što i budžet. Budžet je cilj. Prognoza je očekivana stvarnost.

en.one: Variance is the difference between what you planned and what really happened.
en.explain: If you earn more or spend less than planned, the variance is good (favourable). If you earn less or spend more, it is bad (unfavourable). The point is to ask why.
en.example: You budgeted €500 for ads but spent €700. The variance is €200 unfavourable. Maybe ads got more expensive, or maybe they brought more sales.
en.why: Variances show where the plan was wrong, so next month's decisions get better.
en.mixup: A bad variance is not always a mistake. Spending more on something that works can be the right call.

bs.one: Variance (odstupanje) je razlika između onoga što si planirao i onoga što se stvarno desilo.
bs.explain: Ako zaradiš više ili potrošiš manje od plana, odstupanje je dobro (povoljno). Ako zaradiš manje ili potrošiš više, loše je (nepovoljno). Poenta je pitati zašto.
bs.example: Budžetirao si 500 € za reklame, a potrošio 700 €. Odstupanje je 200 € nepovoljno. Možda su reklame poskupile, a možda su donijele više prodaje.
bs.why: Odstupanja pokazuju gdje je plan bio pogrešan, pa odluke idućeg mjeseca budu bolje.
bs.mixup: Loše odstupanje nije uvijek greška. Potrošiti više na nešto što radi može biti prava odluka.
